# Environment variables

Programs made by BlitzLLVM and the tools read a few environment variables. All of them start with `BLITZLLVM_`, so they do not collide with anything else, and the part after it says what kind of variable it is:

| Name | Kind |
|---|---|
| `BLITZLLVM_LEGACY_<BEHAVIOUR>` | Goes back to what the original Blitz3D or BlitzPlus did, where BlitzLLVM does something else by default. Off by default. |
| `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_<NAME>` | Turns on checks or reports for finding errors or comparing. Off by default. |
| `BLITZLLVM_TEST_<NAME>` | Hooks for the tests of BlitzLLVM itself. Not meant for programs. |
| `BLITZLLVM_<AREA>_<NAME>` | Everything else, grouped by the area it affects (`SPATIAL_GRID`, `ASYNC`, `FULLSCREEN`, `PROFILE`, ...). |

A switch is `1` or `0` (`true`/`false`, `yes`/`no` and `on`/`off` work as well, in any case). Any other value than those that mean no counts as yes, and a variable that is set but empty counts as not set. A switch that is **on** by default is turned off with `0` and has no `NO_` in its name: `BLITZLLVM_SPRITE_HULL=0`. A switch that is **off** by default is turned on with `1`. The runtime reads all of them through one function, so they all work like this.

Variables of the compiler (`blitzcc`) and the tools are read when they start; variables of the runtime are read by the program when it starts, or at the first use of the thing they control.

## Behaviour of the original

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `BLITZLLVM_LEGACY_AUDIO_RESAMPLING` | `0` | Resamples sounds with linear interpolation, like FMOD in the original, see [[Sound-Resampling]]. |

## Settings

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `BLITZLLVM_ASYNC_LOAD` | `0` | Loads pictures and models on other threads, see [[Asynchronous-Loading]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_ASYNC_SAVE` | `0` | Saves pictures on other threads, see [[Saving-Pictures]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_FULLSCREEN_FILTER` | by size | `nearest` or `linear` for the picture of a fullscreen program, see [[Fullscreen]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_FULLSCREEN_SCALE` | smooth | `integer` only enlarges the picture by whole numbers, see [[Fullscreen]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_NETGAME_PORT` | `40500` | The TCP port of multiplayer games, see [[Multiplayer]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_HEADLESS` | `0` | Runs without a window and without sound; dialogs answer with what is safe. For automated runs. |
| `BLITZLLVM_DIALOG_ANSWER` | not set | The number of the button that a dialog presses without being shown, for automated runs, see [[Multiplayer]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_ALLOC_SYSTEM` | `0` | Uses the allocator of the system instead of the one of the runtime, see [[Memory]]. |

## Features that can be turned off

These are on, `0` turns them off, which is useful to compare speed or pictures.

| Variable | What it controls |
|---|---|
| `BLITZLLVM_SPRITE_HULL` | The outline that fits the picture of a sprite, see [[Sprite-Shapes]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_BLEND_DITHER` | Dither 2 through reading the target in the shader (`HWDither`). |
| `BLITZLLVM_DITHER_LOCAL_READ` | Blending in the shader through the local read extensions (only used where the GPU has them). |
| `BLITZLLVM_DITHER_INTERLOCK` | Blending in the shader through the pixel interlock (only used where the GPU has it and the local read extensions are missing or off). |
| `BLITZLLVM_COLLISION_BROADPHASE` | The broad phase of the collisions. |
| `BLITZLLVM_LIGHT_GRID` | The grid that finds the lights that reach a mesh. |
| `BLITZLLVM_LIGHT_CACHE` | Remembering which lights reach a mesh. |
| `BLITZLLVM_SPATIAL_GRID` | The grid that finds the meshes that are in view, see [[Spatial-Grid]]. |

## Tuning

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `BLITZLLVM_SPATIAL_GRID_SCAN_SHARE` | built in | The share of the meshes in the cells that are in view above which the grid is not used for that look, see [[Spatial-Grid]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_SPATIAL_GRID_MAX_MOVED` | built in | How many meshes may move in a frame before the grid is left alone. |

## Debugging and profiling

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_FPS` | `0` | Prints the frames per second and the timers of the runtime once a second. Needs a program made with `--profile` or `-d`. |
| `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_SAMPLE` | not set | The file that receives where the program spends its time (sampled every millisecond). Windows only, needs `--profile`. |
| `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_ALLOC` | `0` | Fills freed and new blocks with patterns and stops when a freed block is written to or freed twice, see [[Memory]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_ALLOC_STATS` | `0` | Counts the blocks and bytes that were not freed and reports them at the end, see [[Memory]]. |
| `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_SYNC_GPU` | `0` | Waits for the GPU after every frame, as if it had no thread. |
| `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_CHECK_LIGHTS` | `0` | Rates the lights of all meshes as well and stops if the grid and the cache gave different ones. |
| `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_SPATIAL_GRID` | `0` | Prints how many meshes the grid found each frame. |

## Compiler and tools

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `BLITZLLVM_CC` | The C compiler `blitzcc` hands the program to. |
| `BLITZLLVM_USERLIBS` | The directory with the user libraries and their `.decls` files, see [[Blitz-Tidy]]. |

## Tests

`BLITZLLVM_TEST_PRESENT`, `BLITZLLVM_TEST_EVENTS`, `BLITZLLVM_TEST_LAYOUT` and `BLITZLLVM_TEST_WINDOW_FLAGS` are read by the runtime and let the tests of BlitzLLVM look at what a window shows and press keys; the test programs and their scripts read a few more (`BLITZLLVM_TEST_PROGRAM`, `BLITZLLVM_TEST_DEBUG`, ...). They can change at any time and are not for programs.

## Old names

Before these names were unified the variables started with `BLITZ_`. The old names still work while the new one is not set, and a program made with `-d` prints a note once for every old name it used. They will be removed; `BLITZ_NO_<FEATURE>=1` is `BLITZLLVM_<FEATURE>=0` now.

| Old name | New name |
|---|---|
| `BLITZ_HEADLESS`, `BLITZ_DIALOG_ANSWER`, `BLITZ_NETGAME_PORT` | `BLITZLLVM_HEADLESS`, `BLITZLLVM_DIALOG_ANSWER`, `BLITZLLVM_NETGAME_PORT` |
| `BLITZ_ASYNC_LOAD`, `BLITZ_ASYNC_SAVE`, `BLITZ_FULLSCREEN_FILTER`, `BLITZ_FULLSCREEN_SCALE` | the same after `BLITZLLVM_` |
| `BLITZ_AUDIO_CLASSIC` | `BLITZLLVM_LEGACY_AUDIO_RESAMPLING` |
| `BLITZ_NO_SPRITE_HULL`, `BLITZ_NO_BLEND_DITHER`, `BLITZ_NO_LOCAL_READ_DITHER`, `BLITZ_NO_INTERLOCK_DITHER`, `BLITZ_NO_BROADPHASE`, `BLITZ_NO_LIGHT_GRID`, `BLITZ_NO_LIGHT_CACHE`, `BLITZ_NO_SPATIAL_GRID` | `BLITZLLVM_SPRITE_HULL=0`, `BLITZLLVM_BLEND_DITHER=0`, `BLITZLLVM_DITHER_LOCAL_READ=0`, `BLITZLLVM_DITHER_INTERLOCK=0`, `BLITZLLVM_COLLISION_BROADPHASE=0`, `BLITZLLVM_LIGHT_GRID=0`, `BLITZLLVM_LIGHT_CACHE=0`, `BLITZLLVM_SPATIAL_GRID=0` |
| `BLITZ_GRID_SCAN_SHARE`, `BLITZ_GRID_MAX_MOVED` | `BLITZLLVM_SPATIAL_GRID_SCAN_SHARE`, `BLITZLLVM_SPATIAL_GRID_MAX_MOVED` |
| `BLITZ_GRID_DEBUG`, `BLITZ_SYNC_GPU`, `BLITZ_CHECK_LIGHTS`, `BLITZ_ALLOC_DEBUG`, `BLITZ_ALLOC_STATS` | `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_SPATIAL_GRID`, `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_SYNC_GPU`, `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_CHECK_LIGHTS`, `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_ALLOC`, `BLITZLLVM_DEBUG_ALLOC_STATS` |
| `BLITZ_ALLOC_SYSTEM` | `BLITZLLVM_ALLOC_SYSTEM` |
| `BLITZ_FPS`, `BLITZ_SAMPLE` | `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_FPS`, `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_SAMPLE` |
| `BLITZ_TEST_PRESENT`, `BLITZ_TEST_EVENTS`, `BLITZ_TEST_LAYOUT`, `BLITZ_TEST_WINDOW_FLAGS` | the same after `BLITZLLVM_` |

One difference to the old behaviour: `BLITZ_HEADLESS` and `BLITZ_AUDIO_CLASSIC` counted as on with any value, also `0`. Now `0` is off.
